purpose: Track public Habr-era technical narratives around Russian Internet restrictions and later YouTube/Google Global Cache explanations, while separating contemporaneous anti-censorship discussion, legitimate CDN degradation, official blame shifting, and any future evidence of coordinated persona/account pre-positioning.

user_lead.claim: The user reports seeing similar talking points/method-like narratives and accounts registered around 2014 that later frame YouTube/Google access problems as Google cluster degradation rather than Russian blocking.
user_lead.required_bridge: Exact handles/profile URLs, registration dates, archived comments/posts and chronology tying the same or coordinated accounts to the technical explanation before or during later restrictions.

link_resolution_note.observed_resolution: Public web retrieval resolved to Habr article 215121, published 2014-03-08: 'Информационно-технологические средства практического выживания социальных сообществ в условиях отключения Интернета в 2014 году'.
link_resolution_note.interpretation: The recovered article is primarily anti-censorship / resilience-oriented, not evidence of a pro-government blame-shifting manual. Do not relabel it as propaganda.

2014_context_confirmed.finding: On 2014-03-08 Habr published a detailed discussion anticipating Russian Internet restrictions, citing planned/actual blocks and discussing resilient communications outside ordinary Internet infrastructure.
The article explicitly mentioned partial YouTube blocking by Russian providers and broader fears of foreign-resource restrictions.

2023_2024_ggc_context.finding: In December 2023 Habr reported that Google offered Russian providers direct peering in Moscow/St Petersburg as an alternative to aging/overloaded Google Global Cache infrastructure; real GGC degradation risk therefore existed as a legitimate technical factor.

On 2024-07-12 Rostelecom publicly attributed YouTube quality problems to Google Global Cache equipment capacity/maintenance issues, and Roskomnadzor said it had nothing to add to that explanation; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia was not considering limiting access and repeated the equipment explanation.
Google later publicly said it was not responsible for the reported YouTube problems in Russia, while Rostelecom continued to attribute them to Google/GGC.

By August 2024 Habr reported YouTube traffic shifting from GGC toward backbone/direct paths and providers supplying GGC connection data to Roskomnadzor; this is inconsistent with treating all observed degradation as a simple single-cause CDN failure.

By November 2024 Rostelecom continued saying it had not technically restricted YouTube and blamed GGC aging, while Habr also reported that Roskomnadzor's GRFC required operators to stop traffic distortion/substitution techniques used against the slowdown and that YouTube had been slowed dramatically versus June levels.

analytic_model.critical_rule: A GGC explanation is not false by definition. Attribution requires measurements showing the observed effect cannot be sufficiently explained by ordinary cache/capacity failure and instead localizes to policy/path intervention.

account_network_question.current_evidence: No independently verified set of Habr accounts registered in 2014 has yet been linked to coordinated repetition of the GGC/Google blame narrative in this pass.
do_not_claim: 2014 Habr accounts were Russian state assets
all GGC-degradation discussion was coordinated propaganda
the 2014 anti-censorship article is itself a propaganda manual
next_evidence_needed: later overlap with known Russian state/SMM infrastructure

outreach_relevance.META: LOW — this is not a Threads integrity issue and should not be added to the Meta complaint.
outreach_relevance.FBI: HIGH AS HISTORICAL TECHNICAL COVER-STORY / ATTRIBUTION-MANIPULATION LEAD IF ACCOUNT COORDINATION IS LATER VERIFIED.
outreach_relevance.ODNI_FMIC: HIGH AS STRATEGIC NARRATIVE PREPOSITIONING / BLAME-SHIFTING MECHANISM.
outreach_relevance.STATE_CFIMI: HIGH AS FOREIGN INFORMATION MANIPULATION AROUND CAUSAL ATTRIBUTION OF ACCESS RESTRICTIONS.
outreach_relevance.CISA: MEDIUM ONLY AFTER TECHNICAL PATH-LOCALIZED EVENT; CURRENTLY HOLD.

current_verdict: The historical/public record supports a real Russian information-control environment by 2014 and a later 2024 dispute in which Russian authorities/operators attributed YouTube degradation to Google/GGC while broader evidence pointed to active Russian network-control intervention. The user's claimed 2014 account/method network remains an important but unverified lead requiring exact account-level evidence before attribution.
